item.title: Brandon Aiyuk Signs With Commanders Practice Squad, Reunites With Jayden Daniels
item.description: Sep 27, 2020; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk (11) runs the ball against New York Giants defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence (97) during the first quarter of a NFL football game at MetLife Stadium. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect For the remainder of the season, Brandon Aiyuk has joined the Washington Commanders practice squad. ESPN ‘s Adam Schefter reported the deal on Wednesday. The 28-year-old wide receiver agreed to a one-year contract after clearing waivers. This move ends his time with the San Francisco 49ers and starts a new chapter in Washington. The signing reunites Aiyuk with quarterback Jayden Daniels, his former teammate from Arizona State. They played together during the 2019 college season. Aiyuk enters the league with a chance to rebuild his career after a two-year absence from game action. His last on-field performance came in 2024 before a knee injury cut his season short. A Fresh Start in Washington The Commanders needed help at the wide receiver position. Star player Terry McLaurin landed on injured reserve, leaving the group thin on depth. Washington now adds Aiyuk to a corps that includes Stefon Diggs, Antonio Williams, and Treylon Burks. The team sits at 4-5-1 on the season, just two games back of the New York Giants for the NFC East lead. Aiyuk brings a proven track record to the roster. Since joining the league in 2020, he has tallied 294 catches, 4,305 yards, and 25 touchdowns. His career-best came in 2023 when he posted 1,342 receiving yards. That performance earned him a second-team All-Pro selection. Before the 2024 season began, he secured a four-year extension valued at up to $120 million with the 49ers. His time in San Francisco ended poorly after the injury. Aiyuk tore his ACL, MCL, and meniscus on Oct. 20, 2024. He missed the entire 2025 season while rehabbing the knee. Conflicting reports surfaced about his health during that long recovery. The distance between player and team grew as the 49ers voided contract guarantees for the 2025 season. Leadership Views on Work Ethic Washington general manager Adam Peters knows Aiyuk well. Peters worked with the receiver in San Francisco from 2020 to 2023. He spoke highly of Aiyuk during a weekly appearance on 106.7 The Fan on Wednesday. Peters called him a “smart football player” and said he was among the 49ers’ “hardest workers on the team”. “One of the things that I don’t think anyone can dispute is his work ethic,” Peters said. He added that this drive is how Aiyuk became an All-Pro-type player. Peters pointed to the 2023 season as proof of his on-field talent. He noted that Aiyuk was a true No. 1 receiver at that time. “He was a true No. 1 receiver at the time. He’s a guy who’s a tough cover, he’s great after the catch. There’s a lot of great things about him on the field,” Peters said. item.title: Trinity Rodman breaks her silence after breakup with Ben Shelton
item.description: Jan 22, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Trinity Rodman of the Washington Spirit wipes a tear during a press conference at BMO Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images One of America’s young power couples has officially called things off, with USWNT star Trinity Rodman and tennis star Ben Shelton reportedly agreeing to go their separate ways after two years together, according to the Daily Mail. Per the outlet, the couple, who began dating around March 2025 and were frequently seen at one another’s sporting events each other, found that long distance and their intesse work schecules made things difficult on their relationship. Rodman, the daughter of NBA legend Dennis Rodman, was a constant presence in Shelton’s box throughout the US Open in September, and she even jetted straight from a game in Washingotn to make it to New York for Shelton’s match in teh final, and was captured cryinginside Arthur Ashe Stadium in the wake of her boyfriend’s loss to Alexander Zverev. Shelton spoke on the difficulties that their schedules presented for their relationship in September. “It is really difficult,” he told US Weekly. “I think what a lot of people don’t see is when we actually do have time or a couple of days off, we’re so exhausted that it’s tough to do anything. It is tough to make time.” “Sometimes I leave these tournaments and I’m a bit of a zombie,” he added. “I’m not the most fun person to be around. But we make a lot of sacrifices for our sport. I’d say both of us are chasing things for our sport. We’re not where we want to be yet, we’re not in our primes. So this is kind of crunch time. “This is going to be the hardest, most grueling time in our relationship, from my perspective. None of it is easy. But being able to have someone to lean on who’s such an elite athlete and doing things at a really high level as well, it helps in so many ways.” “Reset time” On Wednesday, Rodman made her first public comments since news of the split broke via her Instagram story, writing, “Trust the process. Reset time.” Four hours later, Shelton made a post of his own, although his vibes were a lot different, captioning his post with a emoji and added the “Life is Good” remix as the background track. Shelton lost to to Carlos Alcaraz in the semifinal of the ATP Finals in Turin, Italy, on Saturday, but it appears he’s feeling good about where he’s at in life now that he’s single. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Ben Shelton (@benshelton) Rodman also suffered a defeat on Saturday, with her team, the Washington Spirit, losing the NWSL final to the KC Current. She also suffered a shoulder injury within the first few minutes of the final which will cause her to miss the upcoming CONCACAF W Championship tournament for the USWNT. Her time 0ff may be a blessing in disguise, as it’ll allow her the personal time she needs to reflect and reset. item.title: Charles Leclerc ‘hurt’ by accusations of disloyalty after recent spats with Lewis Hamilton
item.description: Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton downplayed tensions ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix after a series of costly and dramatic on-track spats between the Ferrari pair. Leclerc said there was no clause in his new contract giving him number one status at the team, quelling speculation on that topic, and said he was “hurt” by accusations made towards him of disloyalty to Ferrari. The teammates clashed during the Las Vegas Grand Prix on Saturday three weeks on from a high-profile incident in Mexico , prompting Hamilton to urge the Scuderia to clarify their policy on team orders. Speaking ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix, Leclerc said: “The only thing that I don't like seeing is people questioning my integrity to the team, my ⁠love for the team. I've been in Ferrari since ​2019. ⁠I think there's nothing clearer than the love I have for the team, and I will do absolutely everything in order to bring Ferrari back to the top. “Of course, mistakes happen along the way and always will. We just try to minimise them, and particularly between teammates. “I think it's more the question mark that I have seen going around that hurts me more than anything else.” The Monegasque said he was not allowed to discuss possible solutions to the track situation or any rules of engagement - “I cannot disclose that” - but acknowledged the need for a solution. He said: “At the end of the day, we are two very strong drivers that want to finish one ahead of the other. “Unfortunately, it finished recently, whether it's in (Las Vegas) or Monza or Mexico, there's been a bit too many events of those lately, ⁠and we need to find a solution as a team to make sure that these kinds of things don't happen again. “As a team, we cannot afford to clash between teammates, and I think that is very clear for everyone. For the clash in particular of Las Vegas, as I said, I took responsibility. “I think there's just tension around that we just need to dissipate and make sure that we look at more positive days in the future. That's all I'm looking for.” Hamilton was tight-lipped on whether any agreement had been found ahead of the final two races of the season, saying: “We had internal discussions. Everything stays internal. “It's been positive. Charles and I sat here earlier and had a good discussion.” Ferrari are second to champions Mercedes in ‌the constructors’ standings with two races remaining and ​should secure that place in Qatar.

item.title: Carlos Augusto: “I want to keep giving my all for Inter”
item.description: Carlos Augusto: “I want to keep giving my all for Inter” A story that began in 2023 is set for more exciting chapters. To mark his contract extension with Inter until 2031, Carlos Augusto spoke exclusively to Inter TV: Carlos Augusto and Inter together until 2031. How much does this contract extension mean to you? “I’m very happy and grateful for the faith shown in me. I hope to repay the Club on the pitch, as I always have. I hope to keep improving and help Inter stay at the top, winning as much as possible.” You joined Inter at 24 and have since won two Serie A titles, the Coppa Italia and the Supercoppa. What first comes to mind when you look back on what you’ve achieved in Nerazzurri colours so far? “The truth is that time has flown by. In my first season, we earned our second star and it was a special time. When I arrived, I knew the aim was to compete for trophies, and we need to keep doing that. I want to honour the shirt and win as much as possible.” What does wearing the Inter shirt every day mean to you? “It’s an honour to wear this shirt. Inter is one of the best clubs in the world, and I always try to give my all on the pitch to win matches and honour the Nerazzurri shirt.” Game by game, you’ve become a key figure in the team. How do you see the coming years at Inter? “First of all, I need to thank my teammates. They’re the reason I’m able to improve. I’m with them every day, and I’ve been here for a few seasons now. I hope to keep helping Inter stay at the top, because team honours always come before individual ones.” What message do you have for the Inter fans? “I want to thank the fans, who always stand by me. I hope to keep giving my all, stay here for as long as possible and help the team win.”

item.title: Archie Brown could solve Man United’s biggest headache without Ineos blowing their £50m winter kitty
item.description: Archie Brown could solve Man United’s biggest headache without Ineos blowing their £50m winter kitty Not signing a left-back has come back to bite Manchester United. An injury to the club’s only natural left-back, Luke Shaw , has forced them to rely on makeshift options, several of whom have struggled badly. The position has become the Red Devils’ clearest weakness. Last week United chief executive Omar Berrada told Sky Sports : “It’s widely reported we looked for reinforcement in the left-back position… could we have signed an additional defender? Yes, but we have to find the right players at the right value. There’s no point spending £40–50m on players we don’t think improve the team.” As the winter transfer window approaches, United are therefore expected to stick to that transfer principle: They will not sign just any left-back; they want someone who genuinely improves the side. Archie Brown could be that player. The Fenerbahçe left-back has long been linked with Old Trafford, yet United have never acted on their interest. Tempting Archie Brown release clause A golden opportunity has now arisen. German transfer journalist Florian Plettenberg reports that Brown has a €23 million (£19 million) release clause that can be triggered this winter, and the 24-year-old is keen on a move to the Premier League. Man United must seize Archie Brown transfer opportunity United reportedly have a £50 million winter budget, with a striker also viewed as a crucial signing for Mauricio Pochettino. If Ineos are wise and want a successful winter transfer window, they must pounce on Brown. He is athletic, bombs forward down the left flank and thrives in high-tempo football without needing time to adapt to physical duels – ideal for Pochettino’s style. He offers progressive carries, crosses and goals while contributing clearances, interceptions and tackles, making him one of the most complete left-backs available. Securing a player of Brown’s quality for £19 million would be daylight robbery. It would strengthen a major weakness while still leaving room to address other areas, like the attack, as Pochettino fights to keep United in the Premier League.

item.title: Rafael Nadal now explains his famous quote about Nick Kyrgios’ potential in 2019
item.description: “If, If, if… Doesn’t exist.” Those were the words of 22-time Grand Slam champion Rafael Nadal in a press conference after beating Nick Kyrgios in the second round of Wimbledon in 2019, when asked what the then-24-year-old Australian would be capable of achieving if he were to adopt a more professional approach to his tennis career. Nadal had just emerged victorious in their thrilling four-set match at the All England Club, having lost to Kyrgios at the Mexican Open earlier that year. His quote about his opponent that day has since become famous, and he recently expanded on it, two years after retiring from tennis. Photo by Visionhaus/Getty Images Rafael Nadal recalls his comments about Nick Kyrgios Relayed his words back to him in an interview with Brut , Nadal said: “But that’s the truth in the end. I mean, I always heard since I was a kid, if this guy wanted to practice more… so, do it. So that’s the truth, you know. “I think everybody can hide behind an if, you know. And at the end of the day, for me, ‘if’ is a word that is nothing. You did what you did; that’s it, as simple as that. And that’s, yeah, in some way, that’s the way that I understand life. “And that’s the way that I understand my career, you know. Because when I lost because I got injured or when I was not able to play Grand Slam, [people] said, if I was able to play… But I was not able to play. So it’s over. “It doesn’t matter. I lost because I had a problem on my knee. Okay. But I lost. At the end of the day, the result is I lost. It doesn’t matter if it’s because I had or I don’t have. At the end, it’s about results, and that’s the reality. Then it’s always trying to find excuses to find a way to protect yourself.” Photo by Andy Cheung/Getty Images Rafael Nadal’s head-to-head record against Nick Kyrgios Not many players in tennis history can say they beat Nadal once, let alone three times, a tally Kyrgios managed to record. Kyrgios beat Nadal in their first ever clash on the ATP Tour at the 2014 edition of the Wimbledon championships. Aged 19 at the time, wildcard Kyrgios overcame Nadal in four sets to reach the quarterfinals of the grass-court major. Kyrgios became the first man outside the top 100 to beat a world number one at a Grand Slam since 1992. Kyrgios’ second win over Nadal came at the 2017 Cincinnati Open, where he beat him in straight sets to advance to the semifinals of the ATP Masters 1000 event. He bagged his last victory over Nadal in Acapulco in 2019, coming back from a set down to win and make it 3-3 in their head-to-head. The head-to-head ultimately finished 6-3 in favour of Nadal, who won their last three meetings. They were supposed to play for a 10th time in the 2022 Wimbledon semifinals, but Nadal withdrew due to injury.

item.title: Boxing chiefs to assess Fury mental health before fight
item.description: Tyson Fury revealed his schizophrenia diagnosis in a new Netflix documentary [Getty Images] The British Boxing Board of Control is looking into Tyson Fury's comments about his schizophrenia diagnosis but is "fairly confident" the British heavyweight will be cleared to fight Anthony Joshua next month. Fury, 38, is due to face Joshua at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on 11 December, with the ringwalk expected in the early hours of 12 December. In a Netflix documentary out on Friday, he says he heard voices threatening him and his family in the months after he beat Wladimir Klitschko to become world champion in 2015. "We are in the process of dealing with the matter but if there are any medical issues we wouldn't let anyone box, doesn't matter if it's Tyson Fury or not, it could be anybody," Robert Smith, the board's general secretary, told BBC Sport. "I'm fairly confident he will be absolutely fine. We're dealing with it now and we'll have an answer very shortly." Under regulation 8.1(b) of the British Boxing Board of Control's 2026 rules and regulations , schizophrenia is among the conditions that "may preclude" a boxer from obtaining a first licence, while for an existing licence holder the board "may take such action as in its absolute discretion it sees fit". Smith would not say what the process would involve over the next few days, saying "it's a medical matter". He said that all boxers on the card will undergo medical checks, adding: "If our doctors are satisfied he's fit to box, he will box." In the documentary, Fury and his wife Paris recall his admission to hospital in June 2016 with a suspected heart attack. Doctors said he had suffered an anxiety attack. He was diagnosed with schizophrenia after he left hospital, according to the film. The NHS describes schizophrenia as a form of psychosis, and symptoms can include hallucinations, delusions and muddled thoughts and speech. "Words can't explain the darkness I was in," Fury says. The heavyweight, who struggled with drug and alcohol addiction after beating Klitschko, says a Halloween night out in 2017 prompted him to return to training, calling that a "turning point" after being "embarrassed by how I looked". He went on to beat Deontay Wilder in 2020 to become world heavyweight champion for a second time. item.description: Former Real Madrid star heaps praise on Arda Guler: ‘Sees the game before everyone else’ Former Real Madrid star Jorge Lopez Marco, better known as Tote, believes Arda Guler has become an enormously important figure in the team’s attacking play. Speaking on Radio MARCA , the 48-year-old former attacking midfielder highlighted the Turkish international’s exceptional reading of the game and ability to create opportunities for others as qualities that set him apart. Tote’s praise for Guler Tote’s praise for Guler comes after the 21-year-old midfielder signed a new long-term contract with Real Madrid until 2032 . The playmaker has grown into a vital cog in the team’s attacking unit under Jose Mourinho this season, and his form has been key to the team’s ten-game winning run in all competitions. He has already racked up four goals and nine assists from 16 appearances across all competitions for the Spanish capital giants. A key player for Real Madrid. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images) And Tote believes that Guler’s vision sets him apart, allowing Real Madrid to create advantages in the final third and produce a different kind of attacking football when possession goes through him. “He’s the one who sees the game before everyone else,” he said. The former attacker, who spent time at Real Madrid between 1997 and 2001, pointed to Guler’s ability to identify passing opportunities early, provide the final ball and make the team’s attacking movements more effective. Concerns about Real Madrid’s contrasting displays However, Tote also highlighted the contrast between Real Madrid’s performances in different periods of matches, pointing at their performance in the first half and second half during the 5-1 win over PSV. “If another team catches you, you’ll probably go into halftime 0-3 down,” he warned. Tote (R) warned Real Madrid about their slow sart. (Photo by Nuno Correia. Credit: Allsport UK/Allsport) However, he was encouraged by the response after the break as Real Madrid showed greater intensity, moved the ball with more urgency and created more opportunities. The 48-year-old now-retired star also pointed to Kylian Mbappe and Thibaut Courtois as two players who keep making the difference for Los Blancos . “With a goalkeeper and a striker like Real Madrid has, they’re going to fight for everything,” he stated. When asked to name his favourites for the Champions League, Tote suggested that it was too early in the campaign and that the real test will arrive in March and April. “That’s when you see the teams with personality, when you see the winners and those who don’t hesitate.” he explained.

item.title: Raiders QB Fernando Mendoza thankful for Aaron Rodgers on Thanksgiving
item.description: Somewhere in the middle of airing his grievances with the Pittsburgh Steelers on Wednesday, Aaron Rodgers took a moment to say something nice about a fellow quarterback. Imagine Fernando Mendoza’s surprise to find out it was him. Rodgers was on “The Pat McAfee Show” explaining how things had gone sideways with Steelers coach Mike McCarthy when he got around to the Denver film. Pittsburgh plays the Broncos on Friday. The Raiders had just been through Denver on Sunday, which is how a rookie making his second NFL start earned a cameo in somebody else’s very public breakup. Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza (15) throws against the Denver Broncos during an NFL football game in Denver, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. AP Photo/Jack Dempsey “And I’ll tell you: Hey, the kid Mendoza, man. He was running around, making some plays in the scramble.” Funny thing about that tape. If Rodgers goes back to the third quarter and watches what Mendoza did before throwing a 19-yard touchdown pass to tight end Ian Thomas, he might recognize the move the young quarterback busted out. After all, Mendoza borrowed it from Rodgers. The Raiders call it the guitar fake. Watch Mendoza’s hands as running back Ashton Jeanty approached Mendoza as if he was going to be handed the ball. The empty hand carries out the handoff while the other keeps the football tucked against his body. FERNANDO MENDOZA TO IAN THOMAS pic.twitter.com/05xuiDSy3b — wok (@wokdior) November 22, 2026 Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers gestures at a news conference after an NFL football game in Philadelphia, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. AP Photo/Chris Szagola For a beat, the quarterback looks like a guy playing air guitar. By the time Mendoza brings the ball back into view, Thomas is wide open. The extra point tied a game the Raiders once trailed 17-0. It makes sense that any young quarterback would pick out elements of a future Hall of Famer like Rodgers and make them their own. Even more so in the case of Mendoza, who played his first two seasons at Cal, Rodgers’ alma mater. “Yeah, Aaron Rodgers, he also went to Cal, so it’s a little funny, but it was something that we’ve worked on a lot,” Mendoza said. Mendoza spent his last college season at Indiana working primarily from the shotgun, several yards behind the center, with the defense in front of him and the back alongside him. Get under center in Klint Kubiak’s offense, and the view changes in a hurry. Mendoza has to take the snap, turn his back on the defense, meet a runner coming downhill, then get his head around and find his receiver. His feet have to sell the handoff, too. “So, if you don’t have a lot of experience detailing under center handoffs, it’s sometimes hard to then develop the fakes,” Mendoza said. That development adds another layer to a situation that already feels finely balanced. Van Dijk signed a two-year extension in April 2025, taking his deal through to June 2027, yet uncertainty has persisted. The Dutch defender admitted recently that he has “no idea” where he will play next season, a line that naturally intensified interest across Europe and beyond. Trabzonspor move enters early stage The understanding from Turkey is that Trabzonspor are exploring whether a deal is possible, with an apparent preference on their side to try in the winter window. Separate claims have even suggested an offer may already have been put forward, while Van Dijk’s reported valuation stands at €20 million. item.description: Chelsea injury latest: Joao Pedro, Moises Caicedo and more Chelsea Injury Update: Moises Caicedo Fit for Nottingham Forest as Joao Pedro Remains Out Chelsea head to Nottingham Forest on Friday needing points, and needing them quickly. Two straight Premier League defeats, first to Sunderland and then a damaging 4-1 loss at home to Leeds United, have dropped Xabi Alonso’s side to eighth. That is the reality. No spin required. The immediate Chelsea injury update brings one piece of good news and one expected setback. Moises Caicedo is available for the trip to the City Ground after being forced off in the first half against Leeds. Alonso had already admitted the midfielder was “in pain” after that game, but the verdict now is clear. “He is going to be okay for tomorrow.” Joao Pedro Absence Continues Joao Pedro remains out, and Chelsea have felt it. The Brazilian has not featured since the 2-0 win at Everton last month because of a thigh injury. Before that, he had been one of the few sharp edges in Chelsea’s attack, delivering five goals and three assists in the opening six matches of the season. When asked if the forward was fit after being seen at former club Watford in midweek, Alonso’s answer was brief and direct: “No.” There is not much room for interpretation there. Moises Caicedo Return Boosts Midfield Caicedo’s fitness matters because Chelsea have looked loose in midfield without rhythm, protection or control. His own start to the season has been disrupted by injuries, but if he is fit enough to start, Alonso gets back a player who can restore some order in a side that has looked stretched far too often over the last two matches. Maxence Lacroix Recovery Nearer There was less certainty around Maxence Lacroix. The defender suffered a serious hamstring injury against Liverpool and was first expected to be out until January. That timeline now appears to have improved, although not enough for Forest away. Alonso said: “It’s one less week than the last game, so we are closer to the return. But not for this game.” Photo: IMAGO So that is where Chelsea stand. Caicedo back, Joao Pedro still missing, Lacroix not yet ready. After two poor results, excuses are running thin. Friday night now looks straightforward, Chelsea need a response.

item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
